Thus, app-only tokens can be issued without a roles claim.' The same page says Basic auth in the Authorization header 'is also supported' in place of client_secret. So the token succeeds even with zero role assignments, and the downstream ARM GET or PUT returns 403. A successful token at App.tsx:1270, App.tsx:1213 or App.tsx:484 therefore proves the credential is valid and nothing else. It is not a permission check. assumptions.what: Every Azure credential is injected from ONE fixed KV key per host: `Basic ${kv.azureBasic}` (login.microsoftonline.com, line 40), `Bearer ${kv.azureArmToken}` (management.azure.com, line 53) and `Bearer ${kv.azureGraphToken}` (graph.microsoft.com, line 71). Encrypted entries are write-only, so the app can never read one tenant's secret back and copy it into the slot. App.tsx:130-135 says this outright: only one profile's secret can be live at a time.
assumptions.breaksWhen: There is a second tenant whose app registration has its own secret. Any loop over N tenants, such as the dashboard scan, has to put tenant N's client secret into azureBasic before each tenant. Because the app cannot read it back from KV, the operator has to type the secret again for every tenant on every pass. A per-tenant loop that runs unattended cannot be built on this design.
assumptions.fix: Decide this platform question before writing any loop code. Option (a): keep the per-profile client secrets in JS memory for the session only, and before each tenant's batch write that tenant's value to azureBasic, then mint and write the ARM and Graph tokens. Runs must be strictly one tenant at a time behind one mutex. Option (b): store `azureBasic-<profileId>` encrypted, and live-test whether proxies.yml inject expressions can choose a key per request, for example from an allowlisted header. This is unverified. Option (c): a single multi-tenant app registration consented in every tenant, which gives one azureBasic for all tenants, with the tenant set only in the token URL path. That contradicts the stated one-app-registration-per-tenant model and needs a decision. Whichever option is chosen, the change requests must say which secret model is in use.

assumptions.what: PlatformAzureManagement (line 256) and PlatformGraphDirectory (line 434) each keep a `tokenEnsured` boolean per instance. They only mint a new token on the first call or after a 401 (lines 281-293, 461+). The token itself lives in the single shared KV slot (ARM_TOKEN_KV_KEY line 235, GRAPH_TOKEN_KV_KEY line 398).
assumptions.breaksWhen: Two port bundles exist at once, for example the active tenant plus a dashboard loop over tenant B. B writes its token into the shared slot, but A's adapter still has tokenEnsured=true, so A's next request goes out under B's token. Tenant-scoped ARM paths fail with 401 and fall into a re-acquire ping-pong, and concurrent tenants keep evicting each other. Requests that are NOT tenant-addressed succeed silently against the wrong tenant: GET /subscriptions (azure-discovery.ts:230, logging-map-requests.ts:84, azure-resources-section.tsx:226) and Graph /servicePrincipals (adapters.ts:461). The result is tenant B's subscriptions or directory shown under tenant A's name.
assumptions.fix: Track the slot's current owner globally at module scope, holding tenantId+clientId plus the expiry from token.expires_in, instead of a per-instance boolean. Before every send, re-mint the token if the owner is not this adapter's tenant. Serialize all ARM and Graph traffic behind one async mutex shared by all tenants, so a token write and the request that uses it cannot interleave with another tenant's. As defence in depth, check the `tid` claim in the token result against the expected tenantId before writing it.

assumptions.what: Every Sentinel destination references ONE fixed Cribl secret, SENTINEL_CLIENT_SECRET_NAME = 'sentinel_client_secret' (also CRIBL_SECRET_REFERENCE in pack-assembly/outputs-yml.ts:25). wiring-section.tsx:157-162 calls ensureTextSecret with it, and on a 409 for a secret carrying the app stamp it PATCHes the value in place (ensure-text-secret.ts:102).
assumptions.breaksWhen: Tenant B's ingestion secret is entered in the same Cribl worker group. The existing app-owned secret is PATCHed with B's value. Tenant A's Sentinel destinations still carry A's tenantId/clientId but now authenticate with B's secret, so ingestion for tenant A fails with no warning ('Updated existing Cribl secret').
assumptions.fix: Derive the secret id per tenant, for example `sentinel_client_secret_<short tenant/profile token>`. Thread it through destination builds and through outputs.yml, which today hardcodes `!{sentinel_client_secret}`. Before any PATCH, refuse it when the stored secret's description names a different tenant than the caller. Lab FLOWLOG_SECRET_NAME 'Azure_vNet_Flowlogs_Secret' (labs/lab-flowlog-pack.ts:37) has the same fixed-id shape.

assumptions.what: How-to progress is stored under one unscoped KV key, ONBOARDING_PROGRESS_KEY = 'azure-onboarding-progress'. It holds planValues (subscription, RG, namespace, storage account), ticks, workerGroup and criblSources, which is keyed by OnboardingSourceId only (line 86). Those records are this app's KV ownership signal for Cribl inputs (classify-existing.ts:15-17). The first-run seed from config happens only when the key is absent (azure-onboarding-screen.tsx:295-296).
assumptions.breaksWhen: Tenant B opens Azure onboarding and loads tenant A's plan values, ticks and Cribl source records. Saving B overwrites A's document. Once B's criblSources entry for the same source id replaces A's, A's created input loses its KV record, so classifyExistingInput reads it as foreign (not ours) and the dashboard cannot attribute it. A's progress is lost.
assumptions.fix: Scope the key per tenant/profile, for example `azure-onboarding-progress~<tenantId>` (or profile id). Add a one-time migration that assigns the legacy unscoped document to the profile that was active when the migration runs. Prefer tenantId over profile id so that two profiles on one tenant share their facts.

assumptions.what: The coverage selection is stored under one unscoped key, COVERAGE_SELECTION_KEY = 'azure-coverage-selection'. It is loaded and saved at azure-onboarding-screen.tsx:263 and :376.
assumptions.breaksWhen: Every tenant shares one ticked coverage set. The per-tenant dashboard cannot show what each tenant wants, and Save on tenant B overwrites tenant A's selection.
assumptions.fix: Use a per-tenant key (`azure-coverage-selection~<tenantId>`), with the same legacy migration as the progress document. If a tenant-agnostic default template is wanted, keep it as a separate document.

assumptions.what: The screen is mounted without a profile key (App.tsx:2112-2113), unlike the setup sections, which are keyed `connect-${activeProfileId}` (App.tsx:1464, 1499). State that survives a connection switch: `lastRun`, `groupId`, `criblSide`, `rules`. lastResult is reused when the plan values are unchanged (lines 335-337). The load effects re-run only on [store, logger] (lines 282, 310), and store changes identity only when cloudPorts is rebuilt on tenantId.
assumptions.breaksWhen: The operator switches tenant from the connection bar while on this route. Both tenants share one progress document, so the plan values compare equal and tenant A's validation result is shown as tenant B's. The Cribl side and the worker group carry over too. Two profiles with the same tenantId but different clientIds never reload at all.
assumptions.fix: Key the screen like the others: `key={`azure-onboarding-${store.activeProfileId}`}`. Do the same for AzureLoggingMapScreen (App.tsx:2133), although that screen already resets through connectionRef (azure-logging-map-screen.tsx:144-153). Include the tenant in the lastRun guard as well as the plan values.

assumptions.what: cloudPorts is a single bundle memoized only on activeConfig.tenantId (lines 927-930) and spread to every PortsProvider through portsProviderProps (lines 1152-1157). makeCloudPorts (adapters.ts:1856) bakes in a single tenantId. clientId is not in the memo key.
assumptions.breaksWhen: (1) The app can only ever address one tenant, so a dashboard needs a bundle per tenant, which does not exist. (2) Two profiles in the same tenant with different app registrations (different clientId) share one adapter instance and its tokenEnsured state across a switch. That is tolerated today only because applySwitch deletes azureArmToken (lines 1018-1020) and forces a 401 re-mint.
assumptions.fix: Add a shell factory `portsFor(profile)` that returns a memoized Map<profileId, CloudPorts>. Tenant-neutral adapters (cribl, kvDocuments, jobs, samples, content, packs, logger) are shared by reference, and only azure and graph are built per tenant, all over the shared slot mutex described above. Key the memo on tenantId+clientId.

assumptions.what: The secret probe runs once per profile per session (lines 1196-1232). If the `azureBasic` key exists at all, it calls acquireArmToken(activeConfig.tenantId) and on success marks the ACTIVE profile live with the active tenantId/clientId (handleSecretSaved, line 1216). But azureBasic holds whichever profile's secret was saved last.
assumptions.breaksWhen: After a reload with tenant B active, while azureBasic still holds tenant A's credentials. With per-tenant single-tenant apps the probe fails, with a confusing 'failed' notice instead of 'enter B's secret'. If A's app is multi-tenant and consented in B, the probe succeeds and B is shown as live under A's identity, so every later call runs as A's app inside B.
assumptions.fix: Persist (plain KV) a non-secret record of which tenantId/clientId was last written to azureBasic. Probe only when that record matches the active profile, and report 'stored secret belongs to <other connection>' otherwise. azure-profiles.ts:11-12 also claims the secret is 'keyed per profile by the shell', which is false per App.tsx:1252. Correct that doc comment.

assumptions.what: Capability and permission results are stored in ONE KV slot, CAPABILITY_AUDIT_CACHE_KEY = 'capability-audit~v1' (read and written at capability-audit.ts:121 and :145). The stored set carries its capabilityAuditKey, which includes tenant and client (audit-lifecycle.ts:91-104), so it is never misread as another tenant's. But switching tenants overwrites it (use-capability-audit.ts:14-19, capability-audit-state.ts:86-91).
assumptions.breaksWhen: A per-tenant dashboard or least-privilege view would re-measure every tenant on every pass, at roughly a dozen ARM and Cribl probes each, under the shared 100 req/min proxy budget. The earlier tenants' permission results are thrown away, so no view can show 'what tenant N can do' without re-measuring.
assumptions.fix: Store one entry per audit key, for example `capability-audit~v1~<hash(capabilityAuditKey)>` through the hashed contentCache key (contentCacheKvKey, adapters.ts:1317), or a per-tenant document map. loadCachedCapabilities and saveCapabilityAudit take the key as a parameter.

assumptions.what: ARM pacing is per wrapper instance. BATCH_PACING defaults to 80/min (App.tsx:155-163), and paceAzureManagement (onboard-batch.ts:334) creates a new budget for each wrapped port. readLoggingMap paces through its own wrapper (read-logging-map.ts:216). Throttling is per adapter (adapters.ts throttleAware, lines 301-316).
assumptions.breaksWhen: A per-tenant loop that wraps each tenant's port separately, or runs tenants in parallel, gives each wrapper its own 80/min. Two tenants then exceed the platform's roughly 100 req/min proxy budget, and the status poller and other screens starve or get throttled. Parallel tenants also break the single-token-slot invariant.
assumptions.fix: Use one app-scoped pacing budget object shared by every tenant's wrapper: hoist the PollBudget into the shell and pass it in. Run tenants one at a time. Show the dashboard scan as a queued job with per-tenant progress.

assumptions.what: Onboarding Cribl inputs are tagged only with ['azure','azure-onboarding', sourceId] (lines 144 and 199). The Event Hub input body has no tenant at all (lines 136-161), and the blob body has tenantId only as an auth field (line 211). Ids are azure_onb_eh_{ns}_{hub} and azure_onb_blob_{account}_{queue} (lines 78 and 88). These are globally unique only because Azure namespace and account names are, and the 64-char truncation (line 51) can collide, which classifyExisting catches as `differs`.
assumptions.breaksWhen: The dashboard needs 'what is onboarded to Cribl for tenant N'. From the Cribl inputs list alone, an Event Hub input cannot be attributed to a tenant. With the KV progress record shared (see above), there is no attribution left at all. A shared central Event Hub namespace used for two tenants would map both tenants onto one input id.
assumptions.fix: Add a `tenant:<tenantId>` streamtag (or put the tenant in the stamped description) when creating inputs. streamtags is not in IDENTITY_FIELDS, so existing inputs still classify as ours-matching; confirm that against IDENTITY_FIELDS at line 229+. Attribute by tag first and by namespace-to-tenant resolution second.

assumptions.what: Cribl object ids are derived from solution and table only. Pack id is packNameForSolution(prefix, solution) (line 71), and the Sentinel destination id is MS-Sentinel-{table}-dest via destinationId (line 160). Deploy renames a colliding destination to -N, but the pack installer upgrades the pack in place (PATCH) or deletes and retries (adapters.ts:1716-1724).
assumptions.breaksWhen: Tenant B builds and installs the same solution's pack into the same worker group. Its outputs.yml (B's DCR ids, B's tenantId; integrate-screen.tsx:1826, 1858) replaces tenant A's pack in place, and A's routes then deliver into B's workspace. Destinations for the same table get -2 suffixes with no tenant in the name, so the operator cannot tell which belongs to which tenant.
assumptions.fix: Add a tenant token (the profile's short name or the first 8 characters of the tenantId) to the pack id and the destination id whenever more than one profile exists. Refuse an in-place pack upgrade when the installed pack's outputs name a different tenantId.

assumptions.what: 'The' subscription: AzureConfig holds one subscriptionId, resourceGroup and workspaceName per profile (azure-config.ts:49-65). The Defender export (defender-export-section.tsx:107), the Event Hub prerequisite (eventhub-prerequisite-section.tsx:96), defaultPlanValues (plan-values.ts:83-95), the RBAC preflight, DCR inventory, workspace tables and integrate all read config.subscriptionId/workspaceName. ONBOARD_REQUIRED_FIELDS (App.tsx:166-172) requires exactly one of each.
assumptions.breaksWhen: A tenant gap analysis needs every subscription in the tenant (diagnostic settings and Defender continuous export are per subscription), and possibly several Sentinel workspaces. Reading only the configured subscription would mark subscriptions that were never read as not configured.
assumptions.fix: Treat the profile's subscription and workspace as the target workspace only. Gather tenant state through tenant-wide usecases, such as readLoggingMap, which walks managementGroups/{tenantId}/descendants and lists /subscriptions, and report subscriptions that could not be read as unknown, never as red.

assumptions.what: The `started` ref is a boolean set once and never cleared (lines 134-138 and 169). Its own comment (lines 118-133) calls it the single-tenant line that has to change.
assumptions.breaksWhen: A tenant switch rebuilds cloudPorts, which changes loadGroups and re-fires the effect, but the guard swallows it. The data it reloads, though, is Cribl worker groups, Lake datasets and captures from ports.cribl. There is one Cribl workspace per deployment, so the stale list is the same data. The comment's 'one tenant's infrastructure shown under another tenant's name' therefore overstates the consequence today.
assumptions.fix: Store the ports.cribl identity in the ref instead of a boolean (`startedFor.current === ports.cribl`), so a genuinely new Cribl client reloads while an Azure-only change does not. Update the comment so it does not claim Azure-tenant leakage.

assumptions.what: storedCredentialReport reads `azureBasic`/`azureArmToken` presence from a single key listing (lines 429-448) and pairs it with the active profile's tenantId. It already admits 'single shared slot, not per connection'.
assumptions.breaksWhen: It shows 'client secret: stored' for tenant B when the stored secret is tenant A's.
assumptions.fix: Feed it the persisted last-writer record proposed above, and render 'stored for <connection name>'.

assumptions.what: JobRecord (lines 33-52) has no tenant or profile field. jobs-index and pack-builds-index (adapters.ts:584 and 1495) and the tagged-samples index (adapters.ts:768) are app-wide.
assumptions.breaksWhen: Recent runs and pack builds from several tenants show in one list with no way to tell which tenant a deploy hit, unless it happens to be in `input`. Per-tenant audit trails and change-request evidence cannot be filtered.
assumptions.fix: Add an optional `tenantId` (and profileId) to JobRecord, set by the shell's job store wrapper from the bundle's tenant, and filter Recent runs by it. Samples and content cache are tenant-neutral and stay shared.

seams: packages/core/src/usecases/read-logging-map/read-logging-map.ts:149-212 readLoggingMap({ azure, tenantId, now, pacing, onProgress }) - already fully parameterized by port and tenant, with no KV and no config. It is the cleanest per-tenant scan primitive for the 'configured in Azure' half of the dashboard. Call it once per tenant with that tenant's azure port and the shared pacing.

packages/core/src/usecases/capability-audit/capability-audit.ts:53-64,159 runCapabilityAudit(ports: {azure, cribl, cache?, logger?}, input) - ports are passed explicitly, and the result carries capabilityAuditKey (audit-lifecycle.ts:91, which includes tenant and client). It loops per tenant as soon as the cache key is made per-audit-key. It is also the measurement the least-privilege audit and change requests should cite.

packages/core/src/domain/change-request/change-request.ts:51 ChangeRequestContext { appName, config: AzureConfig } - pure and per-config. Generating the Setup page's 'paste comma-delimited TenantIDs' change requests is a map over configs, each built as { ...EMPTY_AZURE_CONFIG, tenantId } plus shared defaults, with no ports and no tokens. This is the one feature that can ship before the token-slot problem is solved.

packages/core/src/domain/azure-profiles/azure-profiles.ts:43-48,154 ProfileStore/upsertProfile - pure helpers, with profile ids minted by the shell (App.tsx:870, 1050).
